description: m5 QED recomputed on single-fragment molecules only, with the single-fragment rate as its stated denominator. Supersedes the whole-SMILES QED in cfm_decode_chemistry_validity.json.
WHY: The panel computed QED on the whole parsed SMILES. RDKit accepts multi-fragment SMILES, so on a fragmented cohort that number scores a bag of fragments rather than a molecule.

correction_magnitude_is_run_dependent.finding: My earlier statement that m5 was 'understated by 39%' was derived from ONE run (cfm_frag_control) and over-generalised. The real pattern is that the contamination scales with the run's own fragmentation rate.

conclusion.low_fragmentation_runs: single_fragment_rate > 0.47 → the whole-SMILES QED is essentially unchanged (−0.2% / +0.1%). No contamination to correct.
conclusion.high_fragmentation_runs: single_fragment_rate ~0.15 → the reported value drops 34-36%. Those runs were flattering the metric by more than half.
conclusion.what_to_quote: qed_single_fragment together with single_fragment_rate. Never qed alone.
conclusion.direction_of_the_fix: the corrected number is WORSE, not better. A metric fix is allowed to make the project look worse; that is the sign it was a fix.

not_the_fix_taken: QED on the largest fragment is also wrong — it reads 0.2718 on cfm_frag_control, HIGHER than both, because taking the biggest piece of a bag of fragments flatters it. Recorded as qed_largest_fragment_all for comparison only.
caution: Every row is a single training run. frag_control (qed_single 0.1246) and frag_assemble (0.1275) differ by less than a seed's worth of variation; do not read a direction into that pair.
